summary:
**Space Mission Design Game** is an interactive 3D space simulation game that makes spacecraft engineering and orbital mission operations engaging through hands-on gameplay. Players take on the role of an astronaut, explore orbital environments in first-person, perform extravehicular activities (EVA), repair satellites, manage oxygen and power resources, and operate spacecraft through an interactive cockpit.

The game combines spacecraft design principles, orbital mechanics, subsystem management, satellite deployment, navigation, and docking challenges into mission-based experiences. Instead of only learning through theoretical explanations or static simulations, players interact with spacecraft systems and experience the consequences of their operational decisions.

By transforming complex aerospace concepts into an immersive, playable environment, the project aims to make space technology more accessible and improve practical understanding of space missions. It provides an engaging way to explore the challenges astronauts and mission operators face, while encouraging interest in aerospace engineering, problem-solving, and space exploration.
details:
Project Details

1. What It Does & How It Works

Space Mission Design Game is a browser-based space simulation and aerospace engineering learning experience. It combines spacecraft design, subsystem engineering, orbital mechanics, and interactive 3D visualisation to help users understand how real space missions are planned and operated.

The project brings together several engineering concepts:

  • Spacecraft Design: Configure modular CubeSats and spacecraft while considering mass, power, battery capacity, propulsion, communication, and thermal constraints.
  • Orbital Simulation: Explore orbital parameters and understand how spacecraft behaviour and mission conditions affect mission outcomes.
  • Mission Simulation: A TypeScript-based simulation engine processes mission events and spacecraft subsystem behaviour through deterministic logic.
  • 3D Visualisation: Three.js and React Three Fiber provide the foundation for interactive spacecraft and space-environment visualisation. Blender models are prepared for integration through the GLB/glTF asset pipeline.
  • Interactive Gameplay: The planned gameplay experience combines first-person astronaut exploration with spacecraft cockpit operations, including EVA activities, satellite interaction, navigation, and docking.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Accessible Aerospace Learning: Makes complex spacecraft engineering concepts easier to explore through an interactive browser-based experience.
  • Practical Understanding: Helps users understand how decisions involving mass, power, propulsion, communication, and orbital conditions influence mission performance.
  • STEM Engagement: Encourages students and space enthusiasts to learn through experimentation, problem-solving, and mission-based challenges.
  • Mission Awareness: Introduces the engineering trade-offs and operational decisions involved in designing and executing space missions.

Our goal is to make space engineering more engaging and accessible by combining scientific concepts with interactive simulation and gameplay.

3. Tools, Languages & Technologies

  • Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS
  • Frontend: Next.js, React
  • 3D Graphics: Three.js, React Three Fiber, WebGL
  • 3D Modelling: Blender
  • 3D Asset Pipeline: GLB/glTF
  • Simulation: Custom TypeScript-based spacecraft and mission simulation engine
  • Development Assistance: Antigravity AI for AI-assisted coding, debugging, implementation, and optimisation
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code and modern web browsers

4. Creativity & Innovation

The project's central innovation is combining aerospace systems engineering with an interactive game experience. Instead of presenting spacecraft engineering only through static diagrams or technical dashboards, it aims to let users explore spacecraft, understand subsystem behaviour, and experience mission operations.

The combination of engineering calculations, deterministic mission events, 3D spacecraft visualisation, and first-person and cockpit-based gameplay creates an engaging way to explore space mission concepts.

5. Key Factors Considered

  • Scientific Reasoning: Use engineering principles and explainable simulation logic rather than arbitrary mission outcomes.
  • Performance: Keep the experience accessible through modern web browsers while considering hardware limitations.
  • Usability: Make complex engineering concepts understandable through interactive controls and visual feedback.
  • Realism: Use Blender-based 3D assets, realistic materials, and appropriate spacecraft proportions.
  • Modularity: Keep spacecraft subsystems and simulation components organised so they can be extended and improved.
  • Learning Experience: Balance technical depth with engaging, mission-oriented gameplay.
